state.constraints: Smallest complete repair for demonstrated legacy gap; preserve permissions/order/atomicity/failure/recovery and owner bounds. No assumption of fresh stores or operational gates. New internal API/marker requires this demonstrated need; no new source syntax. Do not auto-certify an old source table by erasing containment. alternatives.lookup_and_repair: Add a narrow owner-storage lookup for unique claim ownership to memory/D1/DO ports. For contained computed writes, detect relevant raw legacy claims and verify owner row/pure output to distinguish legitimate corrected scoped-key bytes; refuse affected mutation with explicit reindex-required outcome. Add an explicit fenced derived-index repair under the existing trusted activation owner, scanning bounded complete affected rows, validating parent scopes/collisions, releasing old raw claims and claiming scoped values atomically without changing source schema, record data/history/version or permissions. No new persisted version. More implementation than just scope wrapper, but exact legacy gate and repair, and row/claim disambiguation must be proved.
alternatives.version_and_repair: Add a persisted internal computed-index encoding version to installed state/schema, and enforce that version at affected mutation admission. Add explicit existing-owner activation repair that checks complete affected rows/collisions, releases raw and claims parent-scoped values under its resumable fence, and publishes the version atomically. Unversioned populated stores refuse until repaired; fresh stores need checked initialization. Clear lasting gate/no raw-key disambiguation, but new marker threads through installation, fresh-memory/test profiles, storage/activation/admission and recovery.
alternatives.rebuild_each_write: Avoid new port methods or persisted markers by reading all affected model rows under existing owner bounds on every contained computed mutation, validating final grouped parent keys, then atomically releasing all possible old raw/current scoped claims and publishing the complete correct index under the normal revision fence. Automatically repairs old stores and keeps source schema unchanged, but turns indexed writes into full-model computation, must prove releases cannot conflict across namespaces, refuses over bounds and changes runtime cost/evaluation on every write.
